faqs.q: What unique garage door problems do homes in Palatine experience?
faqs.a: Palatine's older housing stock, primarily from the 1970s–90s, often features original garage door components nearing their lifespan. Beyond general wear, the rolling terrain and specific driveway slopes in areas like Deer Grove lead to ice damming. Water and ice collect at the bottom of the garage door during winter, freezing it to the slab. Forcing the door can strip opener gears or snap the trolley. faqs.q: How do Palatine's driveway slopes and winter weather affect garage doors?
faqs.a: Many Palatine homes, particularly those in subdivisions with rolling terrain, have driveways that slope towards the garage door. During winter, snowmelt and rain can drain directly to the door's threshold. When temperatures drop, this water freezes, creating an ice dam. The garage door then becomes frozen solid to the concrete. If you try to open it with the automatic opener, the motor struggles. This commonly results in stripped opener gears or a broken trolley, requiring professional repair.

faqs.q: My garage door in Palatine is frozen shut. What should I do?
faqs.a: If your Palatine garage door is frozen shut, do not force the opener. Attempting to open a frozen door can cause severe damage to the opener motor, gears, or the door's trolley system. This will lead to a more expensive repair. Instead, try to gently chip away any visible ice around the door's bottom seal and threshold. You can also try pouring warm (not boiling) water along the seal. If it remains stuck, call our technicians. We can safely thaw and free your door without further damage.
